references.text: The prophecy that the Messiah would suffer and die for 'the people' (ἔθνους) and 'for sins,' which is directly fulfilled in Caiaphas's prophecy about Jesus dying for the nation.
The description of the suffering servant being 'counted among transgressors' and 'bearing the sins of many,' a theme that Caiaphas unintentionally confirms when he says Jesus must die for the people.
An immediate continuation of the same line of thought, where Jesus not only dies for the nation but also to gather 'God's scattered children' into one.
The New Testament understanding that Christ was offered once to take away sins, parallel to Caiaphas's prophecy that Jesus's death is for the people.
Peter confirms that Jesus 'bore our sins in his body on the tree,' a direct equivalent to Caiaphas's words that Jesus must die 'for the people.'
